subject: Discovery recap & next steps: NebulaPay toolcall + structured outputs
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.in>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nebulapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.in>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps: NebulaPay toolcall + structured outputs

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap so your team can confirm we captured the right priorities and blockers before the demo: 

Pain points you called out
- Current document-to-transaction flow is brittle: JSON output needed from the model must be strictly deterministic for downstream ingestion.
- High tail latency under spiky load (end-of-day reconciliation) impacting batch throughput.
- Data residency requirement for US payment data and a need for audit logs per transaction.

Current stack you shared
- In-house ETL + rules fallback (Node.js)
- Postgres for ledger, hosted in us-east-1
- SAML SSO via Okta
- Inference today: self-hosted LLM (fp16 on A100) with ad-hoc batching and manual fallback to simpler templates

Success criteria you gave
- Deterministic, schema-validated JSON output for every intent type (payments/create, payments/void).
- 99th percentile token latency < 400ms for interactive flows; throughput target ~200 reqs/min during business hour spikes.
- Audit trail and per-request metadata retention for 90 days.

What we propose next (high level)
1) Technical deep-dive with Ben to map the function-call surface and sample payloads (we'll bring a checklist).
2) Demo of a tool-call flow with deterministic JSON output and schema validation (scheduled below).
3) Provide a scoped initial proposal + pricing estimation (attached) and an evaluation bundle (small dedicated pool + instrumented telemetry).

Open questions for you (please reply inline):
- Can you share an anonymized sample set (CSV) of 50 examples we can use to validate the schema and edge cases? (You mentioned an internal QA corpus.)
- Are there regulatory constraints on where inferred partial outputs may be logged? You indicated US-only storage for certain fields.
- Any constraints on acceptable failure modes? (e.g., prefer graceful fallback to template vs. returning a structured error)

Attachments: redwood-inference-initial-proposal.pdf (proposal + eval offer)

Proposed next steps/time:
- Ben/Tech deep-dive: Tue 11/10 10:00–11:00 PT
- Demo (toolcall + schema enforcement): Thu 11/12 09:00–09:45 PT

I'll hold the times and send calendar invites once you confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to working through this.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.in | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nebulapay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.in>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@nebulapay.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps: NebulaPay toolcall + structured outputs

Thanks, Stephanie — great write-up. Confirming a few quick items inline: 

> Can you share an anonymized sample set (CSV) of 50 examples we can use to validate the schema and edge cases?
Yes — we'll export a small sample (sanitized) and attach it. Expect the file by EOD Monday.

> Are there regulatory constraints on where inferred partial outputs may be logged?
We need all personally identifying payment metadata to remain in US-only storage. Non-PII telemetry is fine to store in support buckets.

> Any constraints on acceptable failure modes?
Prefer graceful fallback: when schema validation fails, we want the model to return a deterministic error object (JSON) so our pipeline can handle it without human intervention.

Also, re: throughput — our busiest shard sees ~250 reqs/min during cut-off windows. We may want a small burst buffer.

I'll send the CSV and a short sample of expected JSON keys by EOD (nebula-eval-sample.csv). Please go ahead and send the invites for Tue/Thu.

— Alex
Head of Integrations | NebulaPay
alex.moreno@nebulapay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.in>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nebulapay.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps: NebulaPay toolcall + structured outputs

Looping in a couple of technical clarifications from my side before the deep-dive: 

1) Function / tool-call design - We should define a small set of canonical tool signatures (payments.create, payments.void, dispute.lookup). Each should have an explicit JSON Schema (draft-07) we can enforce server-side.

2) Deterministic formatting success criteria - For evaluation we propose: 97% of test examples must pass strict schema validation with no additional free-text; 99% of required fields populated; error cases return a fixed error object: {"error_type":"validation","missing_fields":[...],"request_id":"<uuid>"}.

3) KV caching + prefix caching - To meet tail latency constraints we can configure prefix cache tokens for common confirmation prompts. We'll bring cache warm-up suggestions to the deep-dive.

4) Attachments / sample schema - Attaching initial schema draft as nebula-schema-v1.json and a short checklist for the deep-dive. Please confirm you received the sample CSV from Alex and we'll run a quick local validation pass ahead of the demo.

I can demo a live run showing the schema enforcement and a fallback error object if you want to see that in the scheduled demo.

— Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.in

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.in>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@nebulapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.in>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.in>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps: NebulaPay toolcall + structured outputs

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick confirmations. Final notes and agenda before our technical deep-dive tomorrow: 

Agenda (30–45m deep-dive)
- Quick infra check: data residency and SSO mapping (Jordan)
- Review nebula-schema-v1.json and map required vs optional fields (Ben)
- Live run: tool-call payments.create against a small eval pool + schema enforcement (Ben)
- Failure mode demo: deterministic error object + pipeline handling (Ben)
- Next steps & evaluation timeline (Stephanie)

Prep list for Nebula team (please bring)
- Anonymized CSV (50 rows) + 5 edge-case examples (nebula-eval-sample.csv)
- Expected JSON keys and business rules (if possible)
- Any compliance/rules on logging PII fields

I've sent invites for: Tue 11/10 10:00 PT (deep-dive) and Thu 11/12 09:00 PT (demo). Links are in the calendar invite; shared docs below.

Shared resources:
- Proposal & eval offer: https://redwood.app/s/NEB-2026-Q4-001
- Demo slot calendar: https://calendar.redwood.com/stephanie/nebula-demo-11-12

We'll validate the sample CSV against nebula-schema-v1.json prior to demo and share a short validation report. If anything changes, flag it in reply to this thread.

Looking forward — Stephanie
